chapter: Reading, repertoire and New Orleans players
title: Kid Rena's drummer and Kid Punch
summary: They recall Chani and Kid Punch, and clubs such as the Pelican and Sam Morgan's.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: And it's... You know... Many a truth is said in jazz. That's what Kid René used to say too. Yeah. He used to say... Who was his drummer? You were talking about his drummer.
I can't think of... Chani. Oh, Chani. Yeah.
Sure. He was wonderful. He played a great kind of beat for that band. 50's, yeah.
Yeah, he and Kid Punch got together after all those.
Kid Punch... Kid Punch played wonderful. Played wonderful plenty. He used to play Pelican Club on all... Mm-hmm. On South Ramp off street. Yeah. Then later on I saw him on Chicago and all.

I used to go on... And... And whenever I get a chance, I go down on... Verone Street and then go back to South Ramp off street. Right to almost the parters. That's where the... Where the... The Parter Club on... Pelican... The Latter Club was upstairs. And they used to play... They had a band there. Kid Punch. Mm-hmm. And Sam... Sam Morgan... He used to play at another one on... Duvaine and then Claiborne... At the San Jacinto Club or something like that. I think... That's where Sam Morgan used to play. But Kid Punch, I love the way he played. I got some... Some of the old records there. Yeah, I love it. I got some of the... The 78 records. Yeah.
